newsitem.title: USA: Seitel unit sees revs up fivefold by 1999.
newsitem.headline: Seitel unit sees revs up fivefold by 1999.

text.p: Seitel Inc's DDD Energy subsidiary expects revenue to rise fivefold by 1999, the company said in a statement after an analysts meeting.

"By 1999, DDD Energy has the potential to approach $100 million in revenue, $30 million in net earnings and $80 million in EBITDA cash flow, based on sustaining a 70 percent drilling success rate," president Horace Calvert said on Friday.
In 1996 revenue was $18.3 million and earnings before income taxes, depreciation and amortization $13.3 million.

These 1999 estimates are based on net daily production nearly tripling to 75 mcf gas per and 4,500 barrels of oil by end-1998 and average pricing of $2.38 per mcf natural gas and $22 per barrel oil and an assumption of a three percent annual rise in prices and operating costs.
DDD's proved reserves at end-1996 rose to 44.9 billion cubic feet equivalent (bcfe) of gas, oil, liquids and sulfur.
It is planning to spend $25 to $30 million in 1997 and participate in the drilling of more than 70 wells of which more than 50 are exploratory prospects.
